newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil sees "better" external accounts in March.
newsitem.headline: Brazil sees "better" external accounts in March.

text.p: Brazil's current account gap and trade figures in March should be "better" than in February, said Altamir Lopes, head of the Central Bank's economics department.
Lopes told reporters the trade balance should improve because of the start of the harvest and higher international commodities prices.
He said pressures on the services account of the balance of payments should also ease, with higher expected remittances by state-owned Banco do Brasil.
"In March, we should have a better trade balance and the pressures on services shouldn't be so strong," Lopes said. "There should be improvement in March."
Brazil's current account deficit for the first two months of 1997 was $4.6 billion compared with a $1.9 billion gap in January to February 1996.
The gap over the past 12 months was equivalent to 3.55 percent of gross domestic product, wider than a revised 3.25 percent of GDP current account deficit posted last year.
Brazil's external financing needs for the 12 months ending February were 2.25 percent of GDP, the highest since October 1995, when the financing needs were 2.35 percent of GDP.
Lopes said he was not worried about the deterioration in the external accounts because it was plainly due to a widening trade deficit.

He said that net foreign direct investment, estimated at at least $12 billion this year after $9.4 billion in 1996, was expected to finance more than 40 percent of the gap this year and the rest would be covered by long-term borrowings.
Short-term volatile portfolio investment was "extra", Lopes said.
Analysts point to a 1997 current account deficit of some $30 billion with financing needs, once direct foreign investment is deducted, at some $20 billion.
Lopes said he was convinced the financing needs would come in at below $20 billion for the year, even though the current account gap might be slightly "worse" than last year's.
